title: Poincaré Duality and Quadratic Refinements over Laurent Rings
abstract: We develop a Poincaré duality theory for defects of nondegenerate sesquilinear pairings over Laurent polynomial rings. A key ingredient is a novel flat resolution of the character module, constructed from a triangulation of the sphere at infinity associated with a fan. The cup product on this resolution turns Poincaré duality on the sphere into canonical pairings between the resulting defect modules. In middle degrees, we construct distinguished quadratic refinements using equivariant cohomology of the sphere with the antipodal action. The effective replacement of the sphere with a projective space provides a geometric substitute for division by two. Applied to translation-invariant Pauli stabilizer codes, our results establish the nondegeneracy of higher-dimensional braiding pairings. They extend the two-dimensional T-junction formula for topological spin to higher dimensions, while giving it a geometric interpretation.
summary: This theoretical paper develops a sophisticated Poincaré duality framework for analyzing defects in quantum lattice models described by Laurent polynomial rings. By constructing canonical pairings and quadratic refinements, the authors extend key topological invariants, such as the topological spin, to higher dimensions. This work provides powerful mathematical machinery for understanding the robustness of topological order in condensed matter systems.
main_problem: The paper develops a Poincaré duality theory for defects of nondegenerate sesquilinear pairings over Laurent polynomial rings.
main_result: It establishes canonical pairings and constructs distinguished quadratic refinements, extending the 2D T-junction formula for topological spin to higher dimensions.
method: The approach combines advanced algebraic topology (Poincaré duality, flat resolutions, equivariant cohomology) with module theory over Laurent rings.
model_or_system: The theory is applied to translation-invariant Pauli stabilizer codes, which model quantum lattice systems and are relevant to topological order and quantum error correction.
key_observables: Duality defects, canonical sesquilinear pairings (Br_p), and quadratic refinements (q or q_L).
important_parameters: The dimension $d$ of the system, and conditions related to the signature $\epsilon(-1)^{d/2}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis often assumes that certain charge modules have finite length, and the construction of quadratic refinements requires specific algebraic conditions.
figures_summary: The text references theorems (A, B, C) and equations detailing the construction of resolutions, pairings, and quadratic forms, particularly relating to the T-junction formula.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing a flat resolution of the character module, then defining the duality defects and pairings, and finally constructing the explicit quadratic refinements using geometric methods.
why_interesting: The connection between abstract algebraic topology (Poincaré duality) and concrete physical models like Pauli stabilizer codes provides deep mathematical tools for understanding topological phases of matter.
